components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 她是一名大三的大学生。
example.pinyin: tā shì yì míng dà sān de dàxuéshēng.
example.english: She is a third-year university student.
example.fact: The University of Bologna, founded in 1088, is generally recognized as the oldest continuously operating university in the world — its original students helped write the "Constitutio Habita" in 1158, a charter that granted traveling scholars legal protection, a founding document of academic freedom still cited today.

examples.hanzi: 我哥哥是一名大学生，在北京读书。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge shì yì míng dàxuéshēng, zài Běijīng dúshū.
examples.english: My older brother is a university student studying in Beijing.

examples.hanzi: 很多大学生暑假会去打工。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō dàxuéshēng shǔjià huì qù dǎgōng.
examples.english: Many college students take part-time jobs in the summer.

components.note: 奏 (zòu) — to play music; as a part it sounds out 揍 zòu and 凑 còu.
攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, as in 教, 放, 收; 效 is to imitate or produce results.
交 (jiāo) — near sound — 效 is xiào; 交 also sounds out 校 xiào and 较 jiào.

example.hanzi: 新的治疗方法很快就奏效了。
example.pinyin: xīn de zhìliáo fāngfǎ hěn kuài jiù zòuxiào le.
example.english: The new treatment method quickly proved effective.
example.fact: Penicillin, discovered accidentally by Alexander Fleming in 1928 when a stray mold contaminated a petri dish, wasn't mass-produced as an effective treatment until the early 1940s — wartime demand during World War II drove production from a few doses to over 646 billion units per year by 1945.

examples.hanzi: 这种药吃下去很快就奏效。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào chī xiàqù hěn kuài jiù zòuxiào.
examples.english: This medicine takes effect soon after being taken.

examples.hanzi: 他的办法没有奏效，问题还是没解决。
examples.pinyin: Tā de bànfǎ méiyǒu zòuxiào, wèntí háishi méi jiějué.
examples.english: His method didn't work, and the problem still isn't solved.

components.note: 危 (danger) — a person at the top of a cliff, with another person kneeling below: a precarious spot.
害 (hài) is a loose sound clue for 割 gē and 辖 xiá; as a word it means to harm, as in 厉害.

example.hanzi: 空气污染会危害人们的健康。
example.pinyin: kōngqì wūrǎn huì wēihài rénmen de jiànkāng.
example.english: Air pollution can harm people's health.
example.fact: The World Health Organization estimates that ambient and household air pollution together contribute to around 7 million premature deaths per year worldwide, making it one of the leading environmental health risks — fine particulate matter smaller than 2.5 micrometers is small enough to pass directly into the bloodstream through the lungs.

examples.hanzi: 吸烟会危害健康。
examples.pinyin: Xīyān huì wēihài jiànkāng.
examples.english: Smoking harms your health.

examples.hanzi: 这些害虫危害了农田里的庄稼。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē hàichóng wēihài le nóngtián lǐ de zhuāngjia.
examples.english: These pests damaged the crops in the fields.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, from 糸) — marks thread and ties, as in 线, 红, 约; 缘 first meant a hem, then the tie of fate.
彖 (tuàn) is only a loose hint for yuán.
古 (gǔ) is a close sound clue for gù; 古 also in 姑 gū and 固 gù.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: an action with a cause.

example.hanzi: 因为天气的缘故，比赛推迟了。
example.pinyin: yīnwèi tiānqì de yuángù, bǐsài tuīchí le.
example.english: Because of the weather, the match was postponed.
example.fact: The strangest weather-related sports disruption on record may be the 1975 English test cricket match abandoned not for rain but for a sudden, unseasonal snowfall in June — groundskeepers had to shovel a covering of snow off the pitch before play could even be considered.

examples.hanzi: 我不知道是什么缘故，他今天没来。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù zhīdào shì shénme yuángù, tā jīntiān méi lái.
examples.english: I don't know the reason, but he didn't come today.

examples.hanzi: 他是因为生病的缘故才请假的。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yīnwèi shēngbìng de yuángù cái qǐngjià de.
examples.english: He took leave because of being sick.

components.note: ⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and walking: 跑, 路, 跳; 跟 first meant the heel, then to follow.
艮 (gèn) is a near sound match for gēn; same part in 根 gēn, 很 hěn, 恨 hèn.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过 pass, 进 enter, 送 send; to follow is to move along behind someone.

example.hanzi: 小狗一直跟随着主人。
example.pinyin: xiǎo gǒu yìzhí gēnsuízhe zhǔrén.
example.english: The little dog kept following its owner.
example.fact: Dogs' ability to track and follow a specific person's scent trail relies on roughly 300 million scent receptors in their nose, compared to about 6 million in humans, and a brain region for processing smell that is proportionally many times larger than ours.

examples.hanzi: 你先走，我随后跟随你。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān zǒu, wǒ suíhòu gēnsuí nǐ.
examples.english: You go first; I will follow you later.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们跟随老师参观了博物馆。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen gēnsuí lǎoshī cānguān le bówùguǎn.
examples.english: The children visited the museum following their teacher.

components.note: 大 (big) — marks size and swagger, as in 太 too, 夺; 夸 is to make something sound big, to boast.
亏 (kuī) hints at the sound: 夸 kuā is close to 垮 kuǎ and 跨 kuà.
将 (jiāng) is the trimmed top part: 奖 jiǎng sounds like 桨 jiǎng and 浆 jiāng.

example.hanzi: 老师在课堂上夸奖了这个学生。
example.pinyin: lǎoshī zài kètáng shàng kuājiǎng le zhège xuésheng.
example.english: The teacher praised this student in class.
example.fact: A well-known 1998 study by psychologist Carol Dweck found that praising children for being "smart" after a task made them perform worse on subsequent challenges than praising their effort or strategy — a finding that reshaped classroom feedback practices around what researchers now call a "growth mindset."

examples.hanzi: 爸爸夸奖我这次考试考得好。
examples.pinyin: Bàba kuājiǎng wǒ zhè cì kǎoshì kǎo de hǎo.
examples.english: Dad praised me for doing well on this exam.

examples.hanzi: 大家都夸奖这位厨师的手艺。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu kuājiǎng zhè wèi chúshī de shǒuyì.
examples.english: Everyone praised this chef's cooking.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and will: 想, 思, 感; 志 is what the heart is set on, ambition.
士 (shì) is only a loose sound hint for zhì.
心 (heart) — wishes and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 愿 is what the heart wants.
原 (yuán) is a close sound clue for yuàn; 原 also in 源 yuán.
者 (zhě) is a sound clue for 都 dū, 著 zhù, 煮 zhǔ, 猪 zhū and 诸 zhū; as a word it means "one who", as in 作者 author.

example.hanzi: 地震发生后，许多志愿者前去救援。
example.pinyin: dìzhèn fāshēng hòu, xǔduō zhìyuànzhě qián qù jiùyuán.
example.english: After the earthquake, many volunteers went to help with the rescue.
example.fact: The 2010 Haiti earthquake relief effort drew tens of thousands of aid workers, and it also marked one of the first large-scale uses of crowdsourced crisis mapping — the open-source platform Ushahidi let volunteers worldwide plot real-time reports of trapped survivors onto a shared map within hours of the disaster.

examples.hanzi: 这家医院正在招募志愿者。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā yīyuàn zhèngzài zhāomù zhìyuànzhě.
examples.english: This hospital is recruiting volunteers.

examples.hanzi: 我周末去养老院当志愿者。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò qù yǎnglǎoyuàn dāng zhìyuànzhě.
examples.english: On weekends I volunteer at a nursing home.

components.note: 龶 (plant-like top) — dictionary reads the top as 'a poisonous plant'. Memory aid: a plant growing on top of a mother (母) is something you must not eat.
母 (mǔ, mother) — the bottom part and radical. Sound clue is lost today (毒 is dú); use it as a visual memory aid, as in 母亲.
糸 (silk, simplified 纟) — undyed silk: plain and basic, hence 元素 element and 素食 vegetarian fare.

example.hanzi: 肝脏能帮助身体排出毒素。
example.pinyin: gānzàng néng bāngzhù shēntǐ páichū dúsù.
example.english: The liver helps the body eliminate toxins.
example.fact: Botulinum toxin, produced by the bacterium Clostridium botulinum, is often cited as the most acutely lethal substance known — yet in minute, carefully controlled doses it's the same toxin used medically as Botox to treat muscle spasms and wrinkles.

examples.hanzi: 烟里含有很多有害的毒素。
examples.pinyin: Yān lǐ hányǒu hěn duō yǒuhài de dúsù.
examples.english: Cigarettes contain a lot of harmful toxins.

examples.hanzi: 多喝水可以帮助排出毒素。
examples.pinyin: Duō hē shuǐ kěyǐ bāngzhù páichū dúsù.
examples.english: Drinking more water can help flush out toxins.

components.note: 钅 (metal; traditional 金) — marks metals, as in 钱 money, 铁 iron, 铜 copper; 铅 is lead, as in 铅笔 pencil.
⺮ (bamboo, 竹字头) — brush shafts were bamboo; also in 笑 smile, 筷 chopsticks.
毛 (hair) — the brush hair at the tip; 笔 is brush and pen.

example.hanzi: 请用铅笔在这张纸上写字。
example.pinyin: qǐng yòng qiānbǐ zài zhè zhāng zhǐ shàng xiězì.
example.english: Please write on this paper with a pencil.
example.fact: Despite the name, pencils have never contained lead; the "lead" is actually a mixture of graphite and clay, a naming holdover from when graphite was first mistaken for a form of lead ore after a large deposit was discovered in Cumbria, England, in the 1500s.

examples.hanzi: 我的铅笔断了，你有削笔刀吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de qiānbǐ duàn le, nǐ yǒu xiāobǐdāo ma?
examples.english: My pencil broke; do you have a sharpener?

examples.hanzi: 他喜欢用铅笔画素描。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan yòng qiānbǐ huà sùmiáo.
examples.english: He likes drawing sketches with a pencil.

components.note: 会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).
合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.

example.hanzi: 我们约好在车站会合。
example.pinyin: wǒmen yuē hǎo zài chēzhàn huìhé.
example.english: We agreed to meet up at the train station.
example.fact: The Apollo 11 mission's most technically delicate moment wasn't the moon landing but the subsequent orbital rendezvous, when the ascent stage carrying Armstrong and Aldrin had to precisely dock with the command module orbiting overhead — a maneuver with no margin for error, since there was no way to rescue the astronauts if it failed.

examples.hanzi: 我们在山脚下会合，然后一起上山。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài shānjiǎo xià huìhé, ránhòu yìqǐ shàngshān.
examples.english: We'll meet at the foot of the mountain and then climb together.

examples.hanzi: 两条河在这里会合。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng tiáo hé zài zhèlǐ huìhé.
examples.english: The two rivers join here.

components.note: 讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talk, as in 说, 话, 请; 诱 is to coax with words.
秀 (xiù) hints at the sound: 诱 yòu is close to 透 tòu and 锈 xiù.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 橱窗里的蛋糕看起来非常诱人。
example.pinyin: chúchuāng lǐ de dàngāo kànqǐlái fēicháng yòurén.
example.english: The cake in the display window looks very tempting.
example.fact: The Venus flytrap lures insects with a sweet, nectar-like scent, but only snaps shut after two separate touch-sensitive trigger hairs are activated within about 20 seconds of each other — a built-in filter that keeps the plant from wasting energy closing on raindrops or debris.

examples.hanzi: 刚出炉的面包闻起来很诱人。
examples.pinyin: Gāng chūlú de miànbāo wén qǐlái hěn yòurén.
examples.english: Freshly baked bread smells very tempting.

examples.hanzi: 他们提出了一个非常诱人的条件。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen tíchū le yí gè fēicháng yòurén de tiáojiàn.
examples.english: They put forward a very attractive offer.

components.note: 干 (dry, shield) — a net 罒 over 干: 罕 first meant a hunting net; it now means rare, as in 罕见 seldom seen.
见 (see) — a big eye on a person's legs 儿: a person looking. The same 见 is in 现 appear, 觉 sense, 视 look.

example.hanzi: 这种鸟在野外非常罕见。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǒng niǎo zài yěwài fēicháng hǎnjiàn.
example.english: This kind of bird is very rare in the wild.
example.fact: The kakapo, a flightless nocturnal parrot native to New Zealand, is one of the rarest birds on Earth: its total population dropped to just 51 individuals in 1995 before an intensive conservation program brought numbers back above 250 by the early 2020s, with every surviving bird individually named and radio-tagged.

examples.hanzi: 这是一种非常罕见的疾病。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yì zhǒng fēicháng hǎnjiàn de jíbìng.
examples.english: This is a very rare disease.

examples.hanzi: 这么大的雪在南方很罕见。
examples.pinyin: Zhème dà de xuě zài nánfāng hěn hǎnjiàn.
examples.english: Snow this heavy is rare in the south.

components.note: 犭 (animal; 犬 dog) — marks animals, as in 猫 cat, 猪 pig, 狗 dog; 狩 is hunting, as in 狩猎.
守 (shǒu) — close sound: 狩 shòu. 守 also sounds out 兽 shòu, which is also an animal word.
犭 (animal, 反犬旁) — beasts and hunting dogs, as in 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狼 wolf.

example.hanzi: 古代人靠狩猎和采集获取食物。
example.pinyin: gǔdài rén kào shòuliè hé cǎijí huòqǔ shíwù.
example.english: Ancient people obtained food through hunting and gathering.
example.fact: Analysis of ancient tools and animal bones suggests early humans were persistence hunters, chasing prey like antelope for hours across open savanna in the midday heat until the animal overheated and collapsed — a strategy made possible by humans' unusually efficient sweating and relatively hairless skin compared with other mammals.

examples.hanzi: 他们在森林里狩猎野兔。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài sēnlín lǐ shòuliè yětù.
examples.english: They hunt hares in the forest.

examples.hanzi: 这个地区禁止狩猎。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dìqū jìnzhǐ shòuliè.
examples.english: Hunting is banned in this area.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 拿; 拉 is to pull.
立 (lì) hints at the sound: 拉 lā is close, as in 垃 lā.
廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).

example.hanzi: 他慢慢拉开了窗帘。
example.pinyin: tā mànmàn lākāi le chuānglián.
example.english: He slowly pulled open the curtains.
example.fact: Modern blackout curtains can block over 99% of incoming light by combining a tightly woven outer fabric with a rubberized or foam backing layer — a design originally developed for wartime blackout regulations in the 1940s to prevent city lights from guiding enemy bombers at night.

examples.hanzi: 他拉开抽屉，找出一把钥匙。
examples.pinyin: Tā lākāi chōuti, zhǎochū yì bǎ yàoshi.
examples.english: He pulled open the drawer and found a key.

examples.hanzi: 请把两把椅子拉开一点。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ liǎng bǎ yǐzi lākāi yìdiǎn.
examples.english: Please pull the two chairs a bit apart.

components.note: 京 (jīng, high mound, capital) is a loose sound clue for jiù; going up to a high place fits 就 "to approach, to go to".
此 (cǐ) is a sound clue for 紫 zǐ, 雌 cí and 些 xiē; as a word it means "this".

example.hanzi: 双方就此达成了协议。
example.pinyin: shuāngfāng jiùcǐ dáchéng le xiéyì.
example.english: The two sides reached an agreement from that point on.
example.fact: The Camp David Accords, signed in 1978 after 13 days of secluded negotiation between Egypt and Israel brokered by U.S. President Jimmy Carter, marked the point from which Egypt became the first Arab nation to formally recognize Israel — a peace treaty that has held for more than four decades since.

examples.hanzi: 这件事就此结束，大家别再争论了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì jiùcǐ jiéshù, dàjiā bié zài zhēnglùn le.
examples.english: Let's end this matter here; stop arguing, everyone.

examples.hanzi: 我们就此告别，希望以后再见。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jiùcǐ gàobié, xīwàng yǐhòu zài jiàn.
examples.english: We say goodbye here, hoping to meet again.

components.note: 木 (wood) — a wooden stick; also in 树 tree, 林 forest.
昆 (kūn) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 混 hùn.

example.hanzi: 他手里拿着一根木棍。
example.pinyin: Tā shǒu lǐ ná zhe yì gēn mùgùn.
example.english: He is holding a wooden stick.
example.fact: The measure word is 根. 光棍 ('bare stick') means a bachelor, and 光棍节 is Singles' Day on 11 November, with its four 'sticks'. 恶棍 is a villain.

examples.hanzi: 老人拄着一根棍子走路。
examples.pinyin: Lǎorén zhǔ zhe yì gēn gùnzi zǒulù.
examples.english: The old man walks leaning on a stick.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们拿棍子在地上画画。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen ná gùnzi zài dìshàng huàhuà.
examples.english: The children draw on the ground with sticks.

meanings: (fig.) first place in a women's competition

components.note: 后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).
广 (building) — 广 is a building or roof, as in 店, 床, 库; 座 is a seat in a hall.
坐 (zuò) — same sound — 座 is zuò, like 坐 (to sit).

example.hanzi: 孩子们坐在汽车的后座上。
example.pinyin: háizimen zuò zài qìchē de hòuzuò shàng.
example.english: The children are sitting in the back seat of the car.
example.fact: Rear-seat seatbelt laws lagged far behind front-seat requirements in most countries — the United States didn't see a major federal push for rear-seat belt use until the 1980s — even though crash studies show unbelted rear passengers can strike front-seat occupants with enough force to injure or kill them too.

examples.hanzi: 我把书包放在了车的后座上。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ shūbāo fàng zài le chē de hòuzuò shàng.
examples.english: I put my school bag on the back seat of the car.

examples.hanzi: 后座的乘客也要系安全带。
examples.pinyin: Hòuzuò de chéngkè yě yào jì ānquándài.
examples.english: Passengers in the back seat must also wear seat belts.

components.note: 水 (water) — a picture of flowing water; as a radical it appears as 氵 on the left (海, 河) or 水 at the bottom (泉, 冰).
中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.

example.hanzi: 鱼在水中自由地游来游去。
example.pinyin: yú zài shuǐzhōng zìyóu de yóu lái yóu qù.
example.english: Fish swim freely back and forth in the water.
example.fact: Water is roughly 800 times denser than air, which is why aquatic animals like whales can grow far larger than any land animal — buoyancy supports their weight so their skeletons don't need to bear the same load a similarly sized land creature's would.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在水中玩得很开心。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài shuǐzhōng wán de hěn kāixīn.
examples.english: The children are having great fun playing in the water.

examples.hanzi: 他在水中憋了一分钟的气。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài shuǐzhōng biē le yì fēnzhōng de qì.
examples.english: He held his breath underwater for one minute.

meanings: see 安寧區|安宁区[An1 ning2 Qu1]
see 安寧市|安宁市[An1 ning2 Shi4]

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.
宀 (roof) — 宀 is a roof, as in 家, 室, 安; 宁 is peace and calm at home.
丁 (dīng) — near sound — 宁 is níng; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng and 厅 tīng.

example.hanzi: 乡村的生活十分安宁。
example.pinyin: xiāngcūn de shēnghuó shífēn ānníng.
example.english: Life in the countryside is very peaceful.
example.fact: Finland topped the UN's World Happiness Report for multiple consecutive years running up to the 2020s, and researchers studying the ranking point to factors like extensive access to nature, low income inequality, and high social trust — Finland has one of the highest ratios of forest and lake area per capita in Europe.

examples.hanzi: 我们希望过上安宁的生活。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xīwàng guò shàng ānníng de shēnghuó.
examples.english: We hope to live a peaceful life.

examples.hanzi: 夜深了，四周十分安宁。
examples.pinyin: Yè shēn le, sìzhōu shífēn ānníng.
examples.english: It was late at night, and it was very quiet all around.

components.note: 力 (strength) — visible inside 为. Memory aid: putting strength 力 into doing something; 为 is 'to do, to act' and, in 因为, 为什么, 'because/for'.
為 (traditional) — often explained as a hand leading an elephant to work. 为 is a cursive simplification, so the picture is no longer visible.
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) — 难 was first the name of a bird; "hard" is a borrowed use. The 又 here stands in for the traditional left part.

example.hanzi: 他的问题让老师有点为难。
example.pinyin: tā de wèntí ràng lǎoshī yǒudiǎn wéinán.
example.english: His question put the teacher in a bit of a difficult spot.
example.fact: The "trolley problem," a thought experiment first posed by philosopher Philippa Foot in 1967, deliberately puts people in an impossible moral bind — divert a runaway trolley to kill one person or let it kill five — and has since become a standard tool for studying real-world ethical dilemmas in fields from medicine to self-driving car design.

examples.hanzi: 别为难他，他也不容易。
examples.pinyin: Bié wéinán tā, tā yě bù róngyì.
examples.english: Don't make things hard for him; it's not easy for him either.

examples.hanzi: 你这样问，让我很为难。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhèyàng wèn, ràng wǒ hěn wéinán.
examples.english: You're putting me in a difficult position by asking that.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 恶 is a bad heart, evil.
亚 (yà) is only a loose sound hint for è.
力 (strength) — 劣 is weak, little strength 少 + 力; poor in quality, as in 恶劣 bad and 劣质 inferior.
少 (few) — 少 + 力: a little strength, so weak or inferior.

example.hanzi: 由于天气恶劣，航班被取消了。
example.pinyin: yóuyú tiānqì èliè, hángbān bèi qǔxiāo le.
example.english: Due to the bad weather, the flight was cancelled.
example.fact: Mount Washington in New Hampshire once recorded a wind gust of 372 km/h in 1934, long considered the fastest surface wind speed ever measured directly by an anemometer — its notoriously severe weather results from storm tracks from the Gulf of Mexico, the Atlantic, and the Pacific all converging over the same small peak.

examples.hanzi: 这里的环境十分恶劣，几乎没有人住。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de huánjìng shífēn èliè, jīhū méiyǒu rén zhù.
examples.english: The environment here is very harsh, and almost nobody lives here.

examples.hanzi: 他的态度恶劣，让客人很生气。
examples.pinyin: Tā de tàidù èliè, ràng kèrén hěn shēngqì.
examples.english: His attitude was bad and made the customer angry.

components.note: 火 (fire) — fire and heat: 灯, 烧, 爆; 炸 is to explode or to fry.
乍 (zhà) sounds exactly like 炸; also in 诈 zhà, 作 zuò, 昨 zuó.
扌 (hand) — hand radical for actions — 掉 is to drop or lose hold.

example.hanzi: 工程队把那座旧桥炸掉了。
example.pinyin: gōngchéngduì bǎ nà zuò jiù qiáo zhàdiào le.
example.english: The engineering crew blew up that old bridge.
example.fact: Controlled demolition engineers use a technique called "implosion," precisely timing hundreds of small explosive charges to detonate in sequence so a building collapses straight down into its own footprint — the technique lets crews safely demolish structures on cramped city blocks without damaging neighboring buildings.

examples.hanzi: 他们决定炸掉那座老桥。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen juédìng zhàdiào nà zuò lǎo qiáo.
examples.english: They decided to blow up that old bridge.

examples.hanzi: 油太热了，把锅都炸掉了一块漆。
examples.pinyin: Yóu tài rè le, bǎ guō dōu zhàdiào le yí kuài qī.
examples.english: The oil was so hot that it blew a patch of paint off the pan.

components.note: 十 (ten/cross) — the visible part; 升 once was a ladle measuring grain, then 'to rise'. The shape does not explain this. Memory aid: a ladle lifted high.
走 (walk, run) — movement, as in 赶 chase, 超 surpass, 越 cross over; 起 is to rise or get up.
己 (jǐ) is a loose sound clue for qǐ; 己 also sounds out 记 jì and 纪 jì.

example.hanzi: 太阳慢慢从东方升起。
example.pinyin: tàiyáng mànmàn cóng dōngfāng shēngqǐ.
example.english: The sun slowly rises from the east.
example.fact: Because Earth's rotation axis is tilted about 23.4 degrees, the exact point on the horizon where the sun rises shifts throughout the year, reaching its northernmost point at the June solstice and its southernmost at the December solstice — ancient structures like Stonehenge were deliberately aligned to track these seasonal extremes.

examples.hanzi: 每天早上，国旗准时升起。
examples.pinyin: Měi tiān zǎoshang, guóqí zhǔnshí shēngqǐ.
examples.english: Every morning the national flag rises on time.

examples.hanzi: 一轮明月从海面上升起。
examples.pinyin: Yì lún míngyuè cóng hǎimiàn shàng shēngqǐ.
examples.english: A bright moon rose from the surface of the sea.

components.note: 钅 (metal, from 金) — marks metals, as in 钱 money, 银 silver, 钢 steel; 铁 is iron.
失 (shī) is only a loose hint for tiě.
⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and travel: 跑, 跳, 跟; 路 is a road.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 洛 luò, 落 luò, 客 kè.

example.hanzi: 这条铁路连接了两座城市。
example.pinyin: zhè tiáo tiělù liánjiē le liǎng zuò chéngshì.
example.english: This railroad connects two cities.
example.fact: The First Transcontinental Railroad, completed in the United States in 1869 at Promontory Summit, Utah, cut coast-to-coast travel time from roughly six months by wagon to about a week by train — its construction relied heavily on thousands of Chinese immigrant workers, particularly on the treacherous Sierra Nevada crossing.

examples.hanzi: 这条铁路已经使用了一百年。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo tiělù yǐjīng shǐyòng le yìbǎi nián.
examples.english: This railway has been in use for a hundred years.

examples.hanzi: 他们在铁路旁边盖了一座房子。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài tiělù pángbiān gài le yí zuò fángzi.
examples.english: They built a house next to the railway.

meanings: in the twinkling of an eye

components.note: 目 (eye) — marks the eyes and seeing, as in 看 look, 睛 eye, 盯 stare; 眨 is blinking, as in 眨眼.
乏 (fá) — loose sound hint (zhǎ vs fá); 乏 means lacking, as in 缺乏.
目 (eye) — sight, as in 看, 睛, 睡.
艮 (gèn) is a loose sound clue for yǎn; 艮 also sounds out 跟 gēn, 很 hěn and 根 gēn.

example.hanzi: 她一眨眼就不见了。
example.pinyin: tā yì zhǎyǎn jiù bùjiàn le.
example.english: In the blink of an eye, she was gone.
example.fact: Humans blink an average of 15 to 20 times per minute — far more often than needed just to keep the eyes lubricated — and researchers have found that a large share of blinks happen at natural pause points during reading or conversation, suggesting the brain uses blinking as a brief, ultra-short mental reset.

examples.hanzi: 他眨眼就把东西吃光了。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhǎyǎn jiù bǎ dōngxi chī guāng le.
examples.english: He finished the food in the blink of an eye.

examples.hanzi: 她向我眨眼，让我别说话。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàng wǒ zhǎyǎn, ràng wǒ bié shuōhuà.
examples.english: She winked at me, telling me not to talk.

meanings: (said of an aging husband) my old man

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 那个老头子每天早上都去公园散步。
example.pinyin: nàge lǎotóuzi měitiān zǎoshang dōu qù gōngyuán sànbù.
example.english: That old man goes for a walk in the park every morning.
example.fact: Jeanne Calment of France holds the verified record for the longest confirmed human lifespan, dying in 1997 at 122 years and 164 days old — she reportedly took up fencing at 85 and continued riding a bicycle until age 100, and her longevity record has stood unbroken for over two decades.

examples.hanzi: 这个老头子很会讲故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhège lǎotóuzi hěn huì jiǎng gùshi.
examples.english: This old man is good at telling stories.

examples.hanzi: 我家那个老头子最爱下象棋。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā nàge lǎotóuzi zuì ài xià xiàngqí.
examples.english: My old man at home loves playing Chinese chess the most.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
钅 (metal; traditional 金) — marks metals, as in 钱, 铁; 钩 is a hook made of metal.
勾 (gōu) — same sound: 钩 gōu. 勾 also sounds out 沟 gōu and 构 gòu.

example.hanzi: 那条鱼终于上钩了。
example.pinyin: nà tiáo yú zhōngyú shàng gōu le.
example.english: That fish finally took the bait.
example.fact: Anglerfish use a bioluminescent lure grown from a modified fin spine that dangles above their mouths, and the light comes not from the fish itself but from colonies of symbiotic bacteria living inside the lure — a partnership that lets the fish attract prey in total darkness thousands of meters below the surface.

examples.hanzi: 鱼儿一上钩，他就赶紧拉线。
examples.pinyin: Yúr yí shànggōu, tā jiù gǎnjǐn lā xiàn.
examples.english: As soon as the fish bit, he quickly pulled the line.

examples.hanzi: 骗子的话你别信，不然你会上钩的。
examples.pinyin: Piànzi de huà nǐ bié xìn, bùrán nǐ huì shànggōu de.
examples.english: Don't believe the con man's words, or you'll take the bait.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 拼 is to put together.
并 (bìng) hints at the sound: 拼 pīn is close to 瓶 píng, which shares it.
囗 (enclosure) — boundaries and surroundings: 国 country, 园 garden, 回 return; 图 is a drawn plan of a region.

example.hanzi: 我们花了三个小时才拼好这幅拼图。
example.pinyin: wǒmen huāle sān gè xiǎoshí cái pīn hǎo zhè fú pīntú.
example.english: It took us three hours to finish this jigsaw puzzle.
example.fact: The jigsaw puzzle was invented around 1760 by London mapmaker John Spilsbury, who mounted a map on wood and cut along country borders to create an educational toy for teaching children geography — the "jigsaw" name only came later, once mechanical jigsaws made cutting interlocking pieces practical for mass production.

examples.hanzi: 孩子喜欢玩一千块的拼图。
examples.pinyin: Háizi xǐhuan wán yì qiān kuài de pīntú.
examples.english: The child likes playing with thousand-piece puzzles.

examples.hanzi: 她用拼图拼出了一幅世界地图。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng pīntú pīn chū le yì fú shìjiè dìtú.
examples.english: She put together a world map with a jigsaw puzzle.

components.note: 兑 (duì) — exchanging or cashing in, as in 兑现 to honour a promise. The part 兑 also sounds out 说 shuō, 税 shuì and 脱 tuō.
王 (jade) — on the left, 王 is the jade radical, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 理 reason; jade is bright and shows itself.
见 (jiàn, see) is a close sound clue (xiàn) and also fits the meaning: appear so it can be seen.

example.hanzi: 他终于兑现了自己的承诺。
example.pinyin: tā zhōngyú duìxiàn le zìjǐ de chéngnuò.
example.english: He finally honored his promise.
example.fact: The world's oldest known written promissory contracts come from ancient Mesopotamia around 2000 BC, inscribed in cuneiform on clay tablets that recorded loans of silver or grain to be repaid by a specified date — an early legal framework for turning a spoken promise into an enforceable, cashable obligation.

examples.hanzi: 他说话算话，一定会兑现诺言。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuōhuà suànhuà, yídìng huì duìxiàn nuòyán.
examples.english: He keeps his word and will definitely fulfill his promise.

examples.hanzi: 这张支票可以到银行兑现。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhīpiào kěyǐ dào yínháng duìxiàn.
examples.english: This check can be cashed at the bank.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — movement, as in 赶 chase, 超 surpass, 越 cross over; 起 is to rise or get up.
己 (jǐ) is a loose sound clue for qǐ; 己 also sounds out 记 jì and 纪 jì.
衤 (clothing) — marks cloth and garments, as in 衬, 衫, 补; 初 pairs it with 刀 knife: cutting cloth was the first step in making clothes, hence 'beginning'.
刀 (knife) — the cutting tool, as in 分 divide, 切 cut.

example.hanzi: 起初他并不相信这个消息。
example.pinyin: qǐchū tā bìng bù xiāngxìn zhège xiāoxi.
example.english: At first, he didn't believe the news at all.
example.fact: Alfred Wegener's 1912 theory of continental drift was met with near-universal rejection by geologists, who found the idea that continents slowly moved across Earth's surface implausible without a mechanism to explain it — it wasn't until the 1960s discovery of seafloor spreading that his originally dismissed idea became mainstream geology.

examples.hanzi: 起初我们都不习惯这里的天气。
examples.pinyin: Qǐchū wǒmen dōu bù xíguàn zhèlǐ de tiānqì.
examples.english: At first we were all not used to the weather here.

examples.hanzi: 起初他很害羞，后来慢慢开朗了。
examples.pinyin: Qǐchū tā hěn hàixiū, hòulái mànmàn kāilǎng le.
examples.english: At first he was shy, but later he gradually became cheerful.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife) on the right, as in 到, 别, 利; 刺 is to stab.
朿 (cì) — 朿 is a thorn and gives the sound — 刺 is cì, same syllable.
乂 (to cut, crisscross) — old for mowing or cutting. Dictionary story: someone cut down 乂 and buried in a wooden coffin 木, a vivid memory aid.
木 (tree, wood) — the bottom. In 杀 it is a leftover of the old 殺 form rather than meaning wood; 殺 also had 殳 (weapon in hand).

example.hanzi: 历史上有很多国王死于刺杀。
example.pinyin: lìshǐ shàng yǒu hěn duō guówáng sǐ yú cìshā.
example.english: Throughout history, many kings have died from assassination.
example.fact: Franz Ferdinand's assassination in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914, succeeded only after an earlier bomb attack that day had failed — his driver then took a wrong turn directly past the same group of conspirators, giving Gavrilo Princip a second, unplanned chance that set off the chain of events leading to World War I.

examples.hanzi: 那位政治家曾经遭到刺杀，但幸运地活了下来。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi zhèngzhìjiā céngjīng zāodào cìshā, dàn xìngyùn de huó le xiàlái.
examples.english: That politician was once the target of an assassination attempt but luckily survived.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影讲的是一场刺杀国王的计划。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎng de shì yì chǎng cìshā guówáng de jìhuà.
examples.english: This movie is about a plot to assassinate a king.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 停 is a person stopping.
亭 (tíng) sounds exactly like 停; same part in 婷 tíng.
留 (liú) is a sound clue for 溜 liū, 榴 liú and 瘤 liú; as a word it means to stay or keep.

example.hanzi: 我们在香港停留了两天。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zài Xiānggǎng tíngliú le liǎng tiān.
example.english: We stayed in Hong Kong for two days.
example.fact: Hong Kong's old Kai Tak Airport was famous among aviation enthusiasts for its approach directly over the rooftops of Kowloon's dense apartment blocks, with pilots making a sharp last-second turn at low altitude before landing — a maneuver retired when the airport moved to its current Chek Lap Kok location in 1998.

examples.hanzi: 火车会在上海停留十分钟。
examples.pinyin: Huǒchē huì zài Shànghǎi tíngliú shí fēnzhōng.
examples.english: The train will stop in Shanghai for ten minutes.

examples.hanzi: 请不要在门口停留，会挡住别人。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng búyào zài ménkǒu tíngliú, huì dǎngzhù biérén.
examples.english: Please don't linger at the door; you'll block others.

components.note: 石 (stone) — 石 as in 破 break, 砖 brick: hard things colliding — 碰 is to bump into.
並 (bìng) — loose hint — 碰 is pèng; 並 (bìng) also sounds out 拼 pīn and 屏 píng.
面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.

example.hanzi: 我们下午三点在图书馆碰面。
example.pinyin: wǒmen xiàwǔ sān diǎn zài túshūguǎn pèngmiàn.
example.english: We're meeting at the library at 3pm.
example.fact: The Library of Alexandria, founded in Egypt around the 3rd century BC, is estimated to have held several hundred thousand papyrus scrolls at its peak and attracted scholars from across the ancient Mediterranean — its gradual decline and eventual loss remains one of history's most cited symbols of how much recorded knowledge can vanish.

examples.hanzi: 明天上午十点我们在公司门口碰面。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān shàngwǔ shí diǎn wǒmen zài gōngsī ménkǒu pèngmiàn.
examples.english: Tomorrow at ten in the morning we'll meet at the company entrance.

examples.hanzi: 好久没见了，找个时间碰面聊聊吧。
examples.pinyin: Hǎojiǔ méi jiàn le, zhǎo gè shíjiān pèngmiàn liáoliao ba.
examples.english: It's been a while; let's find some time to meet and chat.

meanings: (of the people in a group) to get into position (idiom)

components.note: 各 (each) — a foot 夂 arriving at a place 口: each one coming. 各 also sounds out 路 lù, 格 gé, 客 kè and 洛 luò.
京 (jīng, high mound, capital) is a loose sound clue for jiù; going up to a high place fits 就 "to approach, to go to".
各 (each) — a foot 夂 arriving at a place 口: each one coming. 各 also sounds out 路 lù, 格 gé, 客 kè and 洛 luò.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 住.
立 (stand) — the spot where a person 亻 stands 立: a position or seat; also 位置 position.

example.hanzi: 裁判喊道："各就各位，预备，跑！"
example.pinyin: cáipàn hǎndào: "gè jiù gè wèi, yùbèi, pǎo!"
example.english: The referee shouted, "On your marks, get set, go!"
example.fact: Modern Olympic starting blocks are equipped with force sensors that detect a runner's push-off within one-thousandth of a second — since 2010, any sprinter who reacts in under 0.1 seconds after the starting gun is automatically disqualified, since that's faster than the fastest possible human reaction time.

examples.hanzi: 运动员们听到“各就各位”，都蹲了下来。
examples.pinyin: Yùndòngyuánmen tīngdào "gèjiù-gèwèi", dōu dūn le xiàlái.
examples.english: The athletes crouched down when they heard "take your marks".

examples.hanzi: 演出快开始了，大家各就各位。
examples.pinyin: Yǎnchū kuài kāishǐ le, dàjiā gèjiù-gèwèi.
examples.english: The show is about to start, so everyone take your positions.

components.note: 黑 (black) — marks darkness, as in 墨 ink, 黯 dim; 默 mò (silent) sounds like 墨 mò, with 犬 dog quietly following.
大 (big, a person with arms spread) — below carved marks 丰刀: notches cut into tally sticks to record deals, hence contract, as in 契约 and agreement 默契.

example.hanzi: 老搭档之间总有一种默契。
example.pinyin: lǎo dādàng zhījiān zǒng yǒu yì zhǒng mòqì.
example.english: There's always a kind of unspoken understanding between old partners.
example.fact: Studies of elite doubles tennis and volleyball teams have found that long-term partners develop measurably faster nonverbal coordination — reacting to a teammate's body position in as little as 200 milliseconds — a learned synchrony researchers attribute to thousands of hours of shared practice rather than any special innate ability.

examples.hanzi: 我们两个人很有默契，不用多说。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen liǎng gè rén hěn yǒu mòqì, búyòng duō shuō.
examples.english: The two of us have a tacit understanding and don't need to say much.

examples.hanzi: 他们在比赛中配合得很默契。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài bǐsài zhōng pèihé de hěn mòqì.
examples.english: They cooperated with great chemistry in the game.

components.note: 盾 (shield) — a shield held in front of the face; pairs with 矛 spear in 矛盾. 盾 dùn also sounds out 遁 dùn.

example.hanzi: 战士举起盾牌挡住了箭。
example.pinyin: Zhànshì jǔ qǐ dùnpái dǎngzhù le jiàn.
example.english: The soldier raised his shield and blocked the arrow.
example.fact: 盾 is in 盾牌 (shield) and 矛盾 ('spear and shield', contradiction). The idiom 自相矛盾 is from a story of a seller who claimed both unbreakable. Also a currency, as in 越南盾.

examples.hanzi: 盾牌可以保护战士。
examples.pinyin: Dùnpái kěyǐ bǎohù zhànshì.
examples.english: A shield can protect a soldier.

examples.hanzi: 他们两个人之间有矛盾。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen liǎng ge rén zhījiān yǒu máodùn.
examples.english: There is conflict between the two of them.

components.note: 儿 (person, legs) — with 口 mouth on top: the elder brother who speaks for the family. 兄 also in 况 kuàng.

example.hanzi: 他们兄弟两个长得很像。
example.pinyin: Tāmen xiōngdì liǎng gè zhǎng de hěn xiàng.
example.english: The two brothers look very alike.
example.fact: 兄 is more formal than 哥. 兄弟 means brothers and is also a friendly address ('bro'); 老兄 is 'mate'. Also 兄长 (elder brother, respectful).

examples.hanzi: 他是我的兄长。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de xiōngzhǎng.
examples.english: He is my elder brother.

examples.hanzi: 我和他情同兄弟，不分彼此。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hé tā qíng tóng xiōngdì, bù fēn bǐcǐ.
examples.english: He and I are like brothers and don't distinguish between us.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 女 marks women, as in 妈, 姐; 妇 is a married woman.
彐 (hand) — 彐 is a hand holding a broom (the traditional 婦 had 帚), so a married woman who keeps house.

example.hanzi: 这位妇女是我们的邻居。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi fùnǚ shì wǒmen de línjū.
example.english: This woman is our neighbour.
example.fact: 妇 gives 妇女 (women, formal, as in 妇女节 on 8 March), 媳妇 (wife, daughter-in-law), 夫妇 (married couple) and 妇科 (gynaecology).

examples.hanzi: 这位妇女一个人带三个孩子。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi fùnǚ yí ge rén dài sān ge háizi.
examples.english: This woman raises three children alone.

examples.hanzi: 医院里有妇产科。
examples.pinyin: Yīyuàn lǐ yǒu fùchǎnkē.
examples.english: The hospital has an obstetrics and gynecology department.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — the "walk/road" radical appears in characters of going and moving — 过, 进, 送, 逃; here it shows running after something.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads, as in 道 road, 追 chase.
豕 (pig) — the oldest form shows a foot chasing a pig, hence to pursue.

example.hanzi: 猎豹在草原上追逐着猎物。
example.pinyin: liè bào zài cǎoyuán shàng zhuīzhú zhe lièwù.
example.english: The cheetah chases its prey across the grassland.
example.fact: Cheetahs can accelerate from 0 to 100 km/h in about 3 seconds — faster than most sports cars — but their sprints rarely last longer than 30 seconds, since the heat generated by their muscles at top speed would otherwise push their body temperature to dangerous levels.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在草地上追逐打闹。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài cǎodì shàng zhuīzhú dǎnào.
examples.english: The children chase and play around on the grass.

examples.hanzi: 他一生都在追逐自己的梦想。
examples.pinyin: Tā yìshēng dōu zài zhuīzhú zìjǐ de mèngxiǎng.
examples.english: He pursued his dream all his life.

components.note: 阝 (mound, 左耳旁 on the left) — land and hills, as in 院, 阳, 队. The right part is a simplification with no sound clue.
车 (chariot) — war chariots drawn up in a circle (the top part shows the enclosure): an army camp, hence military.

example.hanzi: 他退伍前是陆军上尉。
example.pinyin: tā tuìwǔ qián shì lùjūn shàngwèi.
example.english: Before he retired from the military, he was an army captain.
example.fact: The Terracotta Army buried near Xi'an represents one of history's most detailed records of ancient ground forces: its roughly 8,000 soldiers include distinct infantry, archers, and charioteers arranged in actual military formation, giving archaeologists a rare, precise blueprint of how China's earliest imperial army was organized.

examples.hanzi: 陆军和海军一起进行了训练。
examples.pinyin: Lùjūn hé hǎijūn yìqǐ jìnxíng le xùnliàn.
examples.english: The army and the navy trained together.

examples.hanzi: 他在陆军服役了五年。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài lùjūn fúyì le wǔ nián.
examples.english: He served in the army for five years.

components.note: 戈 (dagger-axe) — marks weapons and cutting, as in 战 battle, 伐 fell; 截 is cutting off a piece, as in 截止 cut-off.

example.hanzi: 请把这张图截下来。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè zhāng tú jié xiàlái.
example.english: Please take a screenshot of this picture.
example.fact: 截 gives 截图 (screenshot), 截止 (cut-off date), 截然不同 (sharply different). It is also a measure word for sections: 一截绳子.

examples.hanzi: 你把这个页面截个图给我。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bǎ zhège yèmiàn jié ge tú gěi wǒ.
examples.english: Take a screenshot of this page and send it to me.

examples.hanzi: 请截止到明天下午五点报名。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jiézhǐ dào míngtiān xiàwǔ wǔ diǎn bàomíng.
examples.english: Please register by five tomorrow afternoon at the latest.
